answer: Charge for inference, not for keys. At epoch open the network issues each identity a salt bound to its own public key; to score, the answer must carry a zk-proof that it is the output of one salted forward pass of the published prompt on a model whose weights hash it names. The salt fixes one vertex of the scoring graph, so no pass serves two identities: N clones need N inferences and N proofs, about two dollars of silicon and copper each, while one honest agent pays once. A hollow shell has no proof behind it.
